title: Winter Light Cathedral
location: Aotea Square, 291-297 Queen Street, Auckland City Centre, Auckland, Auckland
description:
Wander through a glowing tunnel of light and feel the magic of winter come alive!
Step inside Winter Light Cathedral - a dazzling, walk-through experience made from tens of thousands of tiny LED lights. Inspired by the sweeping arches of grand church windows, this luminous tunnel invites you in for a moment of warmth, wonder and a little bit of WOW.
From the outside, it shines like a beacon in Aotea Square. Inside, it’s something else entirely - a sparkling, cosy world where every step surrounds you in soft, golden light.

Walk it once, snap a pic, tag us @aucklandlive, then go again - you’ll want to!

description:

#AucklandRec Meetup number Thirty One is here!

oin us on **Thursday 18 June** for an evening focused on **Trust and Authenticity in Recruitment**.

We’ll be bringing together everyone involved in the recruitment industry to explore one of the biggest topics facing our industry right now: T**rust, verify information, and navigate authenticity** in a hiring market increasingly shaped by A**I, automation, candidate fraud**, and **changing expectations**.

We’ll be joined by **[Holly Whatnall](linkedin.com/in/holly-whatnall) (Talent Acquisition Manager)** **from EY**, who will share insights into what she is seeing across candidate use of AI, GPT-generated resumes and early careers recruitment, alongside **[Will Sloat](linkedin.com/in/will-sloat) from Checkmate**, who will walk through real examples of candidate fraud and verification challenges.

Expect practical insights, real examples, good discussion, and, as always, plenty of fun, laughter and learning with the Auckland recruitment community.

The event will be hosted at the wonderful **Island Recruitment HQ** at the **Spaces offices in Commercial Bay**.

**Event details**
**Date:** Thursday 18 June
**Arrival:** From 5:30pm
**Session starts:** 6:00pm
**Pizza and networking:** From 7:00pm
**Venue:** Island Recruitment HQ / Spaces, Commercial Bay

Join us for plenty of fun, laughter and learning, on 18th June!

title: Babyface
location: Basement Theatre, Lower Greys Avenue, Auckland City Centre, Auckland, Auckland
description:
‘And he's coming in with the steel chair!’ From award-winning writer and performer Nick Tipa (Kāi Tahu), and with dramaturgy by Late Bloomers co-founder Bronwyn Wallace comes Babyface, a solo play about big-time wrestling and small-town Aotearoa.
Whiplash is a professional wrestler and the heavyweight champion of the world. Kahu is a 10-year-old boy and has just moved with his parents to a new town. What do they have in common? They are the same person. Directed by Sara Georgie, and with music and sound design by Zac Nicholls (Koizilla, Space Bats, Attack!), Babyface explores one boy's experience of growing up, fitting in and landing a suplex in rural Aotearoa.
Part stage play / part wrestling show, Babyface, debuted to a sold-out season at Dunedin’s New Athenaeum Theatre as part of the 2025 Dunedin Fringe Festival. Following this, the play took home numerous awards at the Fringe awards night, before also taking the Best Production award at the 2025 Dunedin Theatre Awards.
Awards and nominations:

Winner: Best production - 2025 Dunedin Theatre Awards
Winner: Best concept / script - 2025 Dunedin Theatre Awards
Finalist: Best in Fringe - 2025 Dunedin Fringe Awards
Winner: Unesco City of Literature ‘Beyond Words’ - 2025 Dunedin Fringe Awards
Winner: Theatre Award - 2025 Dunedin Fringe Awards
Winner: Most promising Māori artist (Nick Tipa) - 2025 Dunedin Fringe Awards

"With this solo play, Tipa offers a performance that can’t be missed - his enraptured audience teetering between uproarious laughter and breathless awe at his many comedic and athletic feats." - Ellen Murray, Theatreview
"All in all, Babyface is a fantastic, high energy, very funny show, with a loveable character at its heart." - Brenda Harwood, Otago Daily Times
So paint your signs, put on your favourite wrestling t-shirt, and let's get ready to rrrrrumble!

title: Notes on Tāmaki: WAIWHAI
location: Whare Wānanga, Central City Library, 44-46 Lorne Street, Auckland City Centre, Auckland, Auckland
description:
Descendant of Te Parawhau, Te Uriroroi and Ngāti Mahuta, founder of Noa Records, and inter-dimensional artist, WAIWHAI. (Rāhana Tito-Taylor) walks under the tutelage of many giants in form and spirit from various musical traditions as an exponent of taonga puoro (traditional Maori instruments), psychedelic groove music and avant-garde beats - think Hirini Melbourne meets Sun Ra meets Jeff Parker meets Les Rallizes Dénudés meets Ras G.
WAIWHAI.(fka WhyFi.) has been a trailblazing force within the Tāmaki Makaurau and wider Aotearoa music scene since the mid 2010s, an artist who leans courageously into traditional and iconoclastic tendencies to stretch and weave sound and feeling, summoning spontaneous music that wades between the strange and familiar.
While you are with us on level 2, be sure to check out our Encore! exhibition running from 15 April to 29 August 2026.

title: Sons of Vao
location: ASB Waterfront Theatre, 138 Halsey Street, Auckland City Centre 1010, Auckland
description:
Sons of Vao By Vela Manusaute.
Forged in fire, bound by blood.
“Moving and powerful.” – Adam NZ Play Awards
Vao is a warrior. A charming, handsome man, he carries rage in his fists and danger in his eyes. But, to his three sons, he is a god. “We follow his words and everything he does becomes the law in our young lives. Our lives belong to Vao.”
Spanning four decades, from village life in Niue in the 1970s to the suburbs of Ponsonby, this powerful story follows the brothers’ struggle to break free from their father’s destructive hold.
This play is directed by stage and screen legend Anapela Polata’ivao ONZM (Samoa: Vailoa Faleata, Vaiusu, Fagae’e Safune), who recently starred in the hit movie Tinā and directed acclaimed Auckland Theatre Company works Things That Matter and Red, White and Brass. Audiences can expect a powerfully told story.
A world premiere, Vela Manusaute’s (Niue: Mutalau, Hakupu) autobiographical Adam NZ Play Award-winning script is deeply personal. In parts, it is confronting and, in others, it uses laughter to mask the pain as the brothers emerge into adulthood, carrying childhood scars that affect each of them in very different ways.

title: Agentic AI Evaluation on Bedrock: Lessons from Pushpay's Journey
location: Level 19, Vero Centre, 48 Shortland Street, Auckland CBD, Auckland
description:
Hello everyone,

We're excited to invite you to the **Auckland AWS Tools and Programming meetup**!

This month, we are diving deep into the realities of moving AI from a cool demo to a production-ready system. We are thrilled to host two fantastic co-speakers: **[Roger Wang](https://www.linkedin.com/in/roger-nz/)** (Senior Solutions Architect @ AWS) and **[Saurabh Gupta](https://www.linkedin.com/in/nzsaurabh/)** (Pushpay).

We are gathering once again at the *Pushpay office in the CBD*—looking forward to seeing you all there!

🚨 **Action Required:** To help us streamline building security and sort out the catering (including dietary requirements), please make sure to pre-register before arriving: 👉 **[Pre-register for Venue Check-In Here](https://eventspaces.app/e/build-reliable-agentic-ai-solution-learn-from-pushpay-s-journey-on-agentic-ai-evaluation-f9b80e/register)**

**🎤 The Lineup**
**Roger Wang (AWS) & Saurabh Gupta (Pushpay)**

* **Title:** Breaking Through the 65% Ceiling: How Pushpay Engineered a 95% Accurate Production AI Agent
* **Description:** Agentic AI plateaus fast once you move beyond demos. Pushpay's natural language search agent hit a \~65% accuracy ceiling before the team built a structured evaluation framework to break through it.
Roger and Saurabh will walk through Pushpay's real-world journey: building the agent on **Amazon Bedrock**, why accuracy stalled, and the engineering techniques that pushed it to 95%. They will share practical takeaways including constructing a 300+ query golden dataset, automating measurement with LLM-as-a-Judge, and applying domain-specific prompt engineering on Bedrock. No hype—just real numbers, a real production system, and actionable insights for anyone building or operating agents.
